evidence: src/app/admin/queue/queue.module.ts: @Module({ controllers: [QueueController], providers: [QueueService], imports: [DataGatheringQueueModule, PortfolioSnapshotQueueModule, StatisticsGatheringQueueModule] }), which wires a single admin-queue concern

src/app/admin/queue/queue.controller.ts: @Controller('admin/queue') class QueueController's methods deleteJobs, getJobs, deleteJob and executeJob each call this.queueService.* only, so nothing goes around the module's service

src/app/admin/queue/queue.controller.ts: every endpoint uses @HasPermission(permissions.accessAdminControl) and @UseGuards(AuthGuard('jwt'), HasPermissionGuard), so access control is applied the same way throughout
src/app/admin/queue/queue.controller.ts: deleteJobs and getJobs repeat the status parsing `filterByStatus?.split(',') as JobStatus[]`. This is minor local duplication, not a misplaced invariant
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with one thing: admin control over background job queues. queue.module.ts wires QueueController and QueueService together and imports the three queue modules (DataGatheringQueueModule, PortfolioSnapshotQueueModule, StatisticsGatheringQueueModule) that the service needs. queue.controller.ts exposes job endpoints under 'admin/queue' (deleteJobs, getJobs, deleteJob, executeJob). Every one of those endpoints passes its work to the injected QueueService, so the controller never goes around the module's own service to reach Bull queues directly. Every endpoint also uses the same permission check (@HasPermission(permissions.accessAdminControl) with AuthGuard('jwt') and HasPermissionGuard). Repeating these decorators on each method is normal NestJS practice, not a duplicated invariant. There is one small repeat: deleteJobs and getJobs both turn the status query string into a list with the same line, `filterByStatus?.split(',') as JobStatus[]`. It is trivial input parsing inside one controller, not a business rule split across files, so it doesn't amount to a cohesion failure.
